subject.title: fix(install): validate downloaded scripts before execution

question: Should OpenClaw fail closed when the managed Homebrew or NodeSource setup URL returns content without a raw `#!` prefix, in addition to rejecting download-command failures?
rationale: The source-level failure guards are mechanically justified, but treating a changed trusted upstream script format as an installation-blocking error is a product and security-boundary choice rather than a purely local correctness fix.

options.title: Adopt both guards
options.body: Keep the download-result checks and the raw-shebang validation, accepting that an upstream format change requires an OpenClaw update before installation can continue.

options.title: Limit to transfer failures
options.body: Keep only explicit downloader-result propagation to avoid adding a new content-format availability dependency for trusted upstream scripts.

options.title: Use stronger provenance
options.body: Pause this PR and design a provider-specific authenticated or versioned delivery mechanism if the goal is to verify more than accidental malformed responses.

recommendation.title: Adopt both guards
recommendation.body: Keep the download-result checks and the raw-shebang validation, accepting that an upstream format change requires an OpenClaw update before installation can continue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of the documented installation route makes this the closest available routing candidate; direct installer-history ownership remains unconfirmed.
